newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador denounces Peru's purchase of MiGs.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador denounces Peru's purchase of MiGs.

text.p: Ecuador on Thursday denounced Peru's purchase of 12 MiG combat planes, recalling the border war the two countries fought last year.

"The purchase of such a big number of combat planes and the level of their technical sophistication greatly exceeds Peru's declared intentions and would signify the start of an arms race there," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
"This decision by the Peruvian government is in contrast with the efforts made by the Ecuadoran government to strengthen relations with Peru."
Ecuador early this year purchased four Israeli K-Fir fighter-bombers for $13 million, sparking protests in Peru.

On Wednesday, a top Peruvian military source confirmed to Reuters that Peru had bought 12 Russian MiG 29 fighter planes to replace obsolete jets, some of them irreparably damaged during its month-long war with Ecuador in January 1995.
The U.S. government expressed its displeasure at the purchase of the Migs shortly after the start of formal peace talks in Brasilia between Ecuador and Peru.

The Ecuadoran Foreign Ministry said Peru's rearmament could have serious implications for South America and conflicted with Ecuador's aim to "reach agreements based on trust and transparency in arms purchases."
Ecuador and Peru are carrying out peace talks monitored by the guarantors of the 1942 Rio Protocol peace accord -- Argentina, Brazil, Chile and the United States.
